character_fit.label: Fitness proportions
character_fit.reason: Original straight-arm reach cannot clear the head.

timing.source: declared demonstration tempo; not measured from source photographs

hang_extension.method: fixed bar and limb lengths; bounded lowering for dead hang and measured neutral-chin travel correction, eased by source root height

motion_continuity.method: Measured shoulder-relative elbow path, including loop seam; compare pull and lowering at the same body height.

chin_proxy.method: lowest central 20% / front 40% rigid head rest-surface band; geometric lower-face proxy, not anatomical calibration

pullup_grip_roll.method: One palm-roll branch within 20 degrees of the dead-hang grip; available roll eases with square-root body travel on both strokes.

contacts.grip_source: bounded fit within the photographed grip tolerance

grip_adaptation.method: nearest source grip search within the unchanged dead-hang, wrist and photographed elbow-width limits

rows.note: Reach adaptation changes the photographed equipment path.
Conservative shaft/body surface samples; overlap candidates need visual review.
The lower-face geometric proxy must clear the top of the fixed bar at the top of the rep. Inspect the rendered chin too.
Both elbows must reach at least 175 degrees together at the bottom; a secure grip alone is incomplete movement.
The body moves below a fixed pull-up bar.
Declared whole-body lowering completes the dead hang without stretching the arms or moving the bar.
Any extra body rise to clear the fixed bar must be declared and bounded; the grip and limb lengths stay fixed.
Both elbows must remain below the fixed bar throughout the pull-up.
The forearms must point upward to the fixed grip; an inverted elbow branch is rejected.
At the highest body position the elbows must lie below their shoulders, as in the source pull-up.
Both shoulder-relative elbow paths must remain continuous throughout the pull, lowering and loop seam.
The elbows must follow the same controlled path on the pull and lowering at the same body height.

Folds hidden from every view at the left elbow (up to 273 mm², 4 of 43 frames), the right elbow (up to 245 mm², 9 of 43 frames), the left shoulder (up to 191 mm², 33 of 43 frames) and the right shoulder (up to 165 mm², 24 of 43 frames); plus creases at the elbows, which are normal in deep bends
Generous arm-snap limit; passing this check does not establish exercise technique. Fastest measured joint: elbow.left.
